routes.mechanism: Dismissal and set-aside of a conviction for which probation was not granted

timing.anchorText: more than one year has elapsed since the date of the conviction of a misdemeanor or infraction for which probation was not granted, and the petitioner is not serving a sentence for any offense and is not charged with any crime; relief runs on either of the two routes the Judicial Council form states — that the petitioner has lived an honest and upright life and has obeyed the laws of the land, or that relief is in the interests of justice

Was this a misdemeanor or an infraction?

In which California county were you convicted?
Have you complied with the sentence?
Are you currently serving a sentence or charged with any crime?
Which route applies: you have lived an honest and upright life and obeyed the law, or you are asking in the interests of justice?
Are you a United States citizen?
exclusions: A petitioner who is serving a sentence for any offense, or who is charged with the commission of any crime.
A conviction for which probation was granted, which runs under Cal. Penal Code § 1203.4 and not under this section.
A felony conviction, which this section does not reach.

routes.mechanism: Petition for erasure of cannabis conviction records

timing.anchorText: available on a conviction falling within one of the three categories § 54-142v(a)(1) states — a § 21a-279 conviction for possession of a cannabis-type substance of four ounces or less entered on or after 1 October 2015 and before 1 July 2021, or before 1 January 2000; a § 21a-267(a) conviction before 1 July 2021 for use or possession with intent to use drug paraphernalia for cannabis; or a § 21a-277(b) conviction before 1 July 2021 for a cannabis-type substance of four ounces or less or six plants grown inside the person's own primary residence for personal use — and § 54-142v states no elapsed waiting period of any kind; the court shall direct erasure under § 54-142v(a)(3) if the petition is in order

requiredFacts: What is your full name and date of birth?
Which court, docket number and date of conviction?
Which statute were you convicted under — § 21a-279, § 21a-267(a) or § 21a-277(b)?
What quantity was involved, or how many plants were grown in your own primary residence for personal use?
If this was a paraphernalia conviction, what was the paraphernalia used or intended to be used for?
Is the criminal case still pending?
How many counts are on this docket, and have you confirmed from the record that every one of them is erasable?
Do you have a copy of the arrest record, or will you swear to the quantity in an affidavit?
exclusions: A record referencing more than one count, unless every count is entitled to erasure. § 54-142v(b).
A criminal case that is still pending; the petition does not apply while the case is pending.
A conviction outside the three subsections § 54-142v(a)(1) lists.
The automatic cannabis erasure branch, which runs under § 54-142u for § 21a-279(c) possession convictions inside its own window and is a separate mechanism with no petition.

routes.notes: Void-and-seal under KRS 218A.276 is a different mechanism from expungement under KRS 431.078 or KRS 431.073 and must never be served by either of those pathways: it is available once in a lifetime, it is limited to the three possession offences KRS 218A.276(1) lists, and it turns on completion rather than on an elapsed period. KRS 218A.276(8) to (10) provide that the proceedings may not be used against the defendant except to determine eligibility and that the participant need not disclose them. A participant choosing between void-and-seal and expungement is making a lifetime-consequence strategy decision and is a recorded self-help stop condition, as is any participant who is not a United States citizen, because a voided conviction may still be a conviction for immigration purposes.

routes.mechanism: Removal of a record from the Central Repository after a favourable disposition

timing.anchorText: available at any time after the charge is dismissed, acquittal is entered or disposition of the charge in favour of the person is final; NRS 179A.160(1) states no elapsed waiting period and the only temporal condition is that the favourable disposition be final, after which the Central Repository and the agency shall remove the record unless one of the five conditions in NRS 179A.160(2) applies

requiredFacts: On what date did that outcome become final?
Which agency arrested you, cited you or sought the warrant, on what date, and what case or event number does the record carry?
Does the arrest still show on your Nevada criminal history from the repository?
Was the case resolved through a deferred prosecution, a plea bargain, or any similar arrangement, rather than being dismissed outright or ending in acquittal?
Have you ever been convicted of a felony or a gross misdemeanour anywhere in the United States?
Since the arrest, citation or warrant you want removed, have you been arrested for or charged with any other crime, apart from a minor traffic violation?
What other names have you used, including any former legal names?
exclusions: NRS 179A.160(2)(a): the person is a fugitive.
NRS 179A.160(2)(b): the case is under active prosecution according to a current certificate of a prosecuting attorney.

NRS 179A.160(2)(c): the disposition of the case was a deferred prosecution, plea bargain or other similar disposition. A participant whose case was resolved by a deferral of judgment belongs on the NRS 176.211 track and not here.
NRS 179A.160(2)(d): the person has a prior conviction for a felony or gross misdemeanour in any jurisdiction in the United States, not merely in Nevada.
NRS 179A.160(2)(e): the person has been arrested for or charged with another crime, other than a minor traffic violation, since the arrest, citation or warrant which the person seeks to have removed.
The court's own record, which this application does not reach. Sealing the court record is a separate petition under NRS 179.245 or NRS 179.255 on a different track.
Federal, tribal, military and out-of-state records, which no Nevada application reaches.

routes.notes: A repository remedy, not a court order: the participant applies in writing, no order issues, and NRS 179A.160(3) preserves a court's separate authority to order deletion or modification of a record. It sits alongside the NRS 179.245 and NRS 179.255 court petitions rather than replacing them, which is why the parallel court-record screen is part of the packet. Whether a disposition is favourable to the person is the threshold characterisation on which the whole route turns and the section does not define it; where that is arguable on the record the route stops. Nevada calls this record sealing and never expungement, because it does not authorise destruction of the records.
